David M. Reynolds  
david.m.reynolds@email.com | 555-784-2190 | Seattle, WA

Project Manager with over 15 years of leadership experience driving complex initiatives across diverse industries. Proven ability to translate strategic objectives into actionable plans, leveraging extensive operational and team management expertise honed through a military career. Adept at leading cross-functional teams to deliver projects on time and within budget while fostering collaboration and continuous improvement.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

GlobalTech Solutions, Seattle, WA  
Senior Project Manager | Apr 2017 - Present  
- Directed multiple high-impact projects spanning product development and IT infrastructure upgrades, managing budgets exceeding $12M.  
- Led a cross-departmental team of 25+ personnel, coordinating efforts across product, marketing, and engineering to launch three major software releases in two years.  
- Streamlined project workflows using Agile methodologies, resulting in a 20% improvement in delivery speed.  
- Collaborated with executive leadership to align projects with company-wide strategic goals, enhancing organizational efficiency.  
- Oversaw risk management and mitigation plans that reduced critical project delays by 15%.  
- Mentored junior project managers and team members to build leadership capacity within the organization.

Aegis Defense Systems, Arlington, VA  
Program Manager | Jun 2010 - Mar 2017  
- Managed end-to-end lifecycle of defense-related projects including technology deployment and systems modernization, with a focus on delivering mission-critical solutions.  
- Coordinated multi-disciplinary teams of up to 50 members, effectively translating military operational requirements into actionable civilian business processes.  
- Implemented program controls and reporting mechanisms that improved stakeholder communication and transparency.  
- Led vendor negotiations and contract management that resulted in a 10% cost savings over three years.  
- Facilitated inter-agency collaboration to ensure compliance with federal regulations and standards.  
- Developed training programs to improve team performance and project knowledge transfer.

United States Army, Various Locations  
Operations Officer | Aug 2005 - May 2010  
- Directed comprehensive operational planning and execution for units of 100+ personnel, ensuring mission success under dynamic conditions.  
- Coordinated logistics, personnel, and resource allocation to meet strategic objectives with limited resources.  
- Managed cross-functional teams in high-pressure environments, honing leadership and decision-making skills applicable to civilian project management.  
- Developed after-action reports and operational assessments that informed continuous improvements in tactical and strategic planning.  
- Led training initiatives enhancing team readiness, communication, and problem-solving abilities.  
- Collaborated with multiple government agencies, fostering interdepartmental cooperation and information sharing.

EDUCATION  
Master of Business Administration (MBA), Project Management Focus  
University of Washington, Seattle, WA | Graduated 2015

Bachelor of Science, Business Administration  
Virginia Military Institute, Lexington, VA | Graduated 2005

SKILLS  
- Project Lifecycle Management  
- Agile & Waterfall Methodologies  
- Cross-Functional Team Leadership  
- Risk Management & Mitigation  
- Stakeholder Engagement & Communication  
- Budgeting & Resource Allocation  
- Contract Negotiation  
- Process Improvement  
- Military Operations Planning & Coordination  
- Training & Mentorship

OTHER LINE REWRITES

Useful edits, kept with their own source.

These do not map uniquely to the ranked fixes above, so each stays beside the exact line it rewrites.

LINE EDIT 01 · SOURCE LINE

“- Coordinated logistics, personnel, and resource allocation to meet strategic objectives with limited resources.”

REWRITE

- Coordinated logistics, personnel, and resource allocation across [units or functions] to meet strategic objectives with limited resources; [measurable result]

Add the operational constraint and result that show what your allocation decisions changed.

LINE EDIT 02 · SOURCE LINE

“- Collaborated with executive leadership to align projects with company-wide strategic goals, enhancing organizational efficiency.”

REWRITE

- Collaborated with executive leadership to align [project or portfolio] with company-wide strategic goals, informing [specific decision or deliverable]; [measurable result]

Add the named project decision and organizational result behind the alignment work.

QUESTIONS WORTH ANSWERING

Prompts for your next revision.

These questions are not tied to a specific ranked fix. Use whichever ones surface a true, useful detail.

QUESTION 01

How did translating military requirements at Aegis change a project decision or civilian business process?

Why it may help: This would make the military-to-commercial transition concrete rather than descriptive.

QUESTION 02

What changed when your GlobalTech team expanded across product, marketing, and engineering for three software releases?

Why it may help: The resume gives team size and release count but not the coordination challenge you solved.

QUESTION 03

Which critical delay did your risk plan prevent, and what tradeoff did you make?

Why it may help: The 15% reduction is useful, but the operational judgment behind it is not visible.

QUESTION 04

What workflow changed at GlobalTech, and which Agile practice produced the 20% faster delivery?

Why it may help: This would turn a broad process claim into a repeatable method.

QUESTION 05

During Army operations for 100+ personnel, what decision most affected mission execution under limited resources?

Why it may help: A specific decision would show judgment in the highest-pressure part of your background.

The 20% delivery-speed improvement, 15% reduction in critical delays, and 10% vendor cost savings create a useful record of measurable change.

03

The progression from Army Operations Officer to defense Program Manager to Senior Project Manager makes the career direction easy to follow.

ROLE DIRECTION

Where this story reads strongest.

Position yourself as a senior project or program manager who combines $12M budget ownership, software-release delivery, defense modernization, and military operations planning. Lead with commercial delivery results, then use the military background to reinforce judgment under pressure rather than as the main identity.
